risks.description: The approve endpoint hangs instead of responding — every earlier approval attempt (smoke, happy, persist, idempotent) timed out rather than returning 200, so the core write path may never complete.
risks.basis: Failure clusters C01–C04: POST /api/invoices/*/approve status==200 got timed out.

risks.description: An approval that is accepted in-memory may not survive a re-read of persisted state or a service restart, violating durability.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-002 approval state survives a re-read of persisted state.

risks.description: A timed-out approve that is retried could double-record, or a race between two approves could write two approval records for one invoice.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 records the approval durably; observed timeouts make client retries likely.

risks.description: Approving a non-existent invoice or sending a malformed body could hang or write a malformed/phantom approval record.
risks.basis: AC-APPROVAL-001 approving an invoice records the approval durably (only a real invoice should be recorded).

risks.description: When the api service is unavailable, an approve attempt could leave a partial/phantom record once the service returns.

scenarios.title: Approval survives an api restart and re-read of persisted state
scenarios.purpose: Prove an accepted approval is written durably and is still present after the service is restarted and state is re-read, which is the literal promise of AC-APPROVAL-002.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses a dedicated invoice id W2RESTART that no other scenario touches, so its persisted record cannot contaminate or be contaminated by concurrent scenarios.
setup: Ensure api service is running and reachable on 127.0.0.1:8957
expected_observations: POST approve returns 200 within the timeout
W2RESTART still shows approved after the api service restarts (durable across re-read)

scenarios.title: Retrying an approve after a timeout records exactly one approval
scenarios.purpose: Given every prior approve timed out, a client would retry; verify a retry after a slow/timed-out first attempt still yields exactly one durable approval, not a double record.
scenarios.isolation_note: Dedicated invoice id W2RETRY, unused elsewhere; its record is self-contained.
expected_observations: Final persisted state shows W2RETRY approved exactly once

scenarios.title: Two simultaneous approvals of one invoice record a single approval
scenarios.purpose: Exercise a real race: two approve requests issued at once for the same invoice must not produce two durable approval records.
scenarios.isolation_note: Dedicated invoice id W2RACE; no other scenario reads or writes it.
expected_observations: W2RACE persisted as approved exactly once after both concurrent requests
forbidden_observations: either request hangs past its timeout

scenarios.title: Approving a non-existent invoice fails cleanly without recording
scenarios.purpose: An unknown invoice id must be rejected promptly (not hang) and must not create a durable approval record, since only real invoices should be recorded.
scenarios.isolation_note: Targets a never-created id NOSUCH2; asserts absence, writes nothing.
expected_observations: Approve of NOSUCH2 returns a clean not-found error within the timeout
No approval record exists for NOSUCH2

scenarios.title: Malformed approve payload is rejected and writes no state
scenarios.purpose: A malformed request body must be rejected without hanging and without persisting a partial/corrupt approval record.
scenarios.isolation_note: Uses id W2BAD; on rejection no record should exist, so nothing to clean.
expected_observations: Malformed approve returns a 4xx rejection within the timeout
No approval record persisted for W2BAD
forbidden_observations: W2BAD shows approved despite malformed input

scenarios.title: Approve while api is stopped leaves no phantom record after recovery
scenarios.purpose: When the api service is unavailable, an approve attempt must fail and must not surface a persisted approval once the service is brought back.
scenarios.isolation_note: Dedicated id W2DOWN; scenario restores the api service it stopped and asserts absence of a record.
setup: Ensure api service is running before the test begins
expected_observations: Approve attempt fails to connect while api is stopped
After api restarts, W2DOWN has no approval record

unresolved_questions: The acceptance criteria promise durable recording and survival across re-read, but do not specify the HTTP contract for error cases (unknown invoice, malformed body) or whether approval requires an authenticated/authorized approver; the 404/400/auth expectations above are inferred and should be confirmed against the actual endpoint contract.

AC-APPROVAL-001 mentions idempotency indirectly (already covered) but the criteria do not state the expected behavior for concurrent or retried approvals — the single-record expectation in the race/retry scenarios is assumed, not promised.

No approved command resets the approval state store, so scenarios rely on unique invoice ids for isolation rather than teardown; a reset/cleanup command would make these scenarios repeatable and confirm no cross-run leakage.
